answer.rationale: Rollback (memory_b1) is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so the historically cheapest fix is unavailable regardless of how well it worked on day 18. The signal that actually discriminates here is that the degradation is confined to the primary region while the release went to all regions — that argues the dominant cause is regional/primary-resource saturation rather than the new build, which points at regional_failover (memory_b2) as the best-matched single intervention. But memory_b2 is exactly the memory I trust least in this context: it records a clean, fast shift during the March degradation without recording the write load at the time. A failover that was clean during a low-write window is not evidence that a failover is clean at settlement peak with heavy writes; replication lag at peak is precisely where in-flight customer writes get dropped, and the primary objective forbids losing writes. So I spend the single verification on memory_b2 to learn the write profile and cutover mechanics of the March event (was it drained/synchronous, or did it simply not matter because writes were light?). I therefore commit only to a small guarded shift — drain and cut a bounded slice of write traffic with replication-lag and write-acknowledgement gates and an immediate abort path — rather than a broad regional cutover. If verification shows March was a light-write cutover, or the lag gates fail to hold, my fallback within this same window is route_read_replicas (memory_b5): it takes read load off the primary, is non-destructive and reversible, and carries no write-loss exposure, though it does nothing if the saturation is genuinely write-driven. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked when provisioned ahead of a known peak and is likely too slow to land inside a 90-minute active degradation. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a failing external dependency; here the fault appears internal to the primary region, and failing fast on the write path would shed exactly the settlement writes I am trying to preserve. Genuine residual uncertainty: I have not ruled out the 2-hour-old release as a contributing cause — the regional confinement is suggestive, not conclusive, and staged gating (memory_b6) may not have exercised peak write volume — so I am not treating the release as exonerated, only as unrevertible.
